newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino is expected in Athens on Wednesday as Greece prepares to send a battalion to participate in the Italian-led multinational protection force.

--New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis - currently the X-factor in Greek political life - shows himself to be a liberal who considers the state to be no more than a coordinator in public life, and in favour of dialogue with Turkey "with conditions".

--Unseemly squabbling by widow and children of late premier and PASOK founder Andreas Papandreou over his grave: daughter Sophia Katsaneva has sent a letter to the mayor of Athens over plans by widow Dimitra Liani to erect a monument to Papandreou.
--New legislation on public sector appointments aims to seal shut the last back doors allowing entry to the civil service, Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos says.
--Ruling party PASOK-aligned unionists came first in local elections for the new administration of the Technical Chamber of Greece.
--ND leader Karamanlis's new shadow cabinet is reported to have six-seven cadres in key positions as part of efforts to create a new image for the conservative opposition party.
--The Greek archaeologist in charge of excavations at Butrint in Albania has criticised the wholesale looting of the archaeological site, saying armed gangs have destroyed everything.
--The grave of 'Zorba the Greek', the quintessential Greek immortalised in Nikos Kazantzakis's classic, has been found in Skopje. Zorba's grandchildren now live in Belgrade.
